title: BRING THE FIRST AND THE BEST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When you have entered the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance and have taken possession of it and settled in it, take some of the firstfruits of all that you produce from the soil of the land the Lord your God is giving you and put them in a basket." — Deut 26:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Israel had even crossed into the promised land, God was teaching them how to live once they arrived. Notice the order of things here. First God gives, then the people respond. The land was an inheritance, not wages. They had not earned it; they were simply receiving what God had promised. And their response to His giving was to bring back to Him the firstfruits — the very first and best of the harvest.

There is something deeply freeing in this. When we understand that everything we hold is first a gift from God's hand, giving back to Him stops feeling like loss and starts feeling like worship. The farmer who trusted God brought the first basket, not the leftovers, because he believed more was coming from the same faithful God.

For us today, this is not a rule about crops. It is a heart posture. Do we give God our leftover time, leftover energy, leftover attention — or the first and the best? Christ gave us His very best when He gave Himself (Eph 5:2). In light of such a gift, we bring Him our firstfruits gladly, not grudgingly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I tend to give God my first and best, or my leftovers?
2. What would it look like to offer God the "firstfruits" of my day this week?
3. How does remembering that everything is a gift change the way I give?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that everything I have first came from Your generous hand. Teach me to bring You my first and my best, not out of duty but out of love. Amen.
